body.translated_text: Now begins the <s>Karatoyāmāhātmya</s> (Glory of the Karatoyā River).

children.translated_text: O Lord, let there be told further,
especially regarding the rivers,
the greatness of the <s>Pauṇḍra</s> sacred land
has not been heard in detail, O Master.
When was her origin, and how?
And why is she especially distinguished?
I wish to hear, O <s>Bhūteśa</s> (Lord of Beings),
if there be grace upon me.
By whom was she made manifest,
that river <s>Karajā</s> (born from the hand), upon the earth?
And how was the sacred land inundated,
the auspicious and unsurpassed <s>Pauṇḍra</s>?
At the time of your wedding ceremony,
O <s>Devī</s>, by <s>Himavat</s> (the Himalaya) water
was offered, and from my hand
it flowed forth as <s>Karajā</s> upon the earth.
All this has been told before,
regarding <s>Pauṇḍra</s>, O <s>Sureśvarī</s> (Queen of the Gods),
and there itself was told to you
the merit of <s>Karatoyā</s>.
And now, regarding those rivers
especially,
she who is holy and removes the sins of <s>Kali</s> (the dark age)
was made manifest by <s>Bhārgava</s> (Paraśurāma).
My son <s>Guha</s> (Skanda) also
dwells there always,
where the Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s> abides,
<s>Īśvara</s> (the Supreme Lord) seated upon <s>Garuḍa</s>.
Always and with complete devotion,
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> <s>Hari</s> is in <s>Pauṇḍra</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> does not forsake <s>Puṣkara</s>,
nor do I forsake <s>Vārāṇasī</s>,
and the sacred land of <s>Śrīpauṇḍravardhana</s>,
<s>Keśava</s> never abandons.
The navel-lotus of the earth
is purified by the waters of my hand.
Listen, O sages all,
to what was spoken by <s>Bhārgava</s> indeed,
having heard from <s>Śaṅkara</s> the words,
the dialogue between the two.
Out of affection for his son,
it was revealed to <s>Bhārgava</s>,
and that illustrious <s>Bhārgava</s> himself
made it known to the sages.
Salutation to that chief of sages,
the slayer of the lord of demons,
to the glorious <s>Cakrapāṇi</s> (Wielder of the Discus),
who is the Self of <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śiva</s>.
Alone, with only his axe,
having slain the <s>Kṣatriyas</s> in battle,
he made the earth devoid of <s>Kṣatriyas</s>
twenty-one times.
Therefore he is known as <s>Paraśurāma</s> (Rāma with the Axe),
famed for his valor upon the earth,
<s>Jāmadagnya</s> (son of Jamadagni), of great prowess,
whose existence was at the beginning of <s>Tretā</s> (the second age).
Omniscient, of excellent vows, pure,
the establisher of all righteous conduct,
his heart drawn by wonder,
the supreme <s>Hari</s> upon the earth.
In <s>Pauṇḍra</s>, at <s>Koṭiśilādvīpa</s>,
of great holiness and wide renown,
the water of the river <s>Karatoyā</s>,
which purifies the body from beginning to end,
for the sake of the fruits of devotion and liberation,
by whom offerings were made to the <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>.
A wondrous creation was performed
of gold for three days,
between <s>Skanda</s> and <s>Govinda</s> (temples),
the land became a consecrated altar.
On the northern side of the altar's center,
the goddess <s>Kālañjarī</s> is established,
to its south is installed the goddess
known as <s>Koṭīśvarī</s>.
In the southwest, crores of <s>liṅgas</s>
were installed by <s>Bhṛgu</s>,
in the west stands <s>Vijayā Caṇḍī</s>,
and in the north, <s>Bhūtikeśvara</s>.
Having bathed in that <s>kuṇḍa</s> (sacred pool) on an auspicious day,
a person is freed from sin.
To the south of the deity <s>Bhūtikeśvara</s>
is a pavilion of <s>Sūrya</s> (the Sun).
In the center of the altar a sacrificial post is installed,
and by touching it, the merit of men increases.
To the east of the <s>Govinda</s> pavilion
is a <s>kuṇḍa</s> (sacred pool) built by <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
To the northwest of the <s>Skanda</s> pavilion
is the wondrous assembly hall of <s>Rāma</s>,
where one hundred and twenty-five thousand <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>
of wondrous deeds reside.
By the power of the austerities, O <s>Devī</s>,
of that great-souled chief of sages,
that assembly hall stands, and in the northwest corner
is a pit fashioned by <s>Īśvara</s> (the Lord).
The primeval abode of the earth, with one hundred and twenty-five thousand <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,
graced by <s>Skanda</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Balabhadra</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and other deities,
its sins washed away by the waters born of the hand,
I bow my head to the city of <s>Śrīpauṇḍravardhana</s>.
On the western side of <s>Karajā</s>,
the <s>Jāhnavī</s> (Ganges) flows always,
and on the eastern side flows <s>Karajā</s>,
with waters a quarter less than the <s>Jāhnavī</s>.
On the western bank of <s>Karatoyā</s>,
where the reddish soil is found,
the field of liberation is proclaimed,
which destroys the greatest sins.
Having reached the river <s>Karatoyā</s>,
a person who fasts for three nights
obtains the fruit of an <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice)
and goes to the world of <s>Śakra</s> (Indra).
And having attained knowledge here itself,
one may attain union with <s>Hari</s>.

body.text: COMM.: e. atraiva: corr., atrava ed. Cf. vs. 46.

children.translated_text: Those who, having reached <s>Karatoyā</s>,
give up their mortal body,
for them there is liberation without doubt,
for as long as fourteen <s>Indras</s> reign.
They are not mere humans but gods,
those who drink from three rivers:
<s>Devikā</s>, <s>Karatoyā</s>,
and <s>Vipāśā</s>, the destroyer of sins.
Between <s>Skanda</s> and <s>Govinda</s> (temples),
on a Monday falling on the new moon day,
one who bathes at dawn in silence
uplifts ten million generations of his lineage.
How many grains of dust are there on the earth?
How vast is what is born of the sky?
The greatness of <s>Karatoyā</s>
can never be fully told.
The merit obtained from beholding <s>Puruṣottama</s>
at the time of the great full moon of <s>Jyaiṣṭha</s>,
that same fruit one obtains
by bathing in the waters of <s>Karatoyā</s>.
Having reached the waters of <s>Karatoyā</s>,
if the new moon falls on a Monday,
at the time of dawn,
it equals hundreds of solar eclipses.
Having reached <s>Śilādvīpa</s>,
the merit becomes ten million-fold,
and that same is multiplied ten million-fold again
when it falls with the sun in <s>Pauṣa</s>.
Whatever merit there is in <s>Vārāṇasī</s> or <s>Kurukṣetra</s>
at the sight of <s>Rāhu</s> (during an eclipse),
having reached <s>Śilādvīpa</s>,
that becomes ten million-fold.
In the month of <s>Pauṣa</s> or <s>Māgha</s>,
if the new moon falls on a Monday,
with the <s>Vyatīpāta</s> conjunction,
the merit becomes ten million times ten million-fold.
When the sun is in Sagittarius, conjoined with <s>Mūla</s> (nakṣatra), if the new moon falls on a Monday,
it is celebrated as <s>Nārāyaṇī</s> (tithi),
and one uplifts thirty million generations of one's lineage.
Worship performed in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>
bestows complete fruit,
yet twice that is declared
in the waters of the river <s>Karatoyā</s>.

body.text: COMM.: b. saṃpūrṇa-: corr., samparṇa- ed.

children.translated_text: In <s>Dvāravatī</s>, at the <s>Gaṇḍakī</s>,
at <s>Prayāga</s>, at <s>Puṣkara</s> likewise,
at <s>Badarī</s>, at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>,
whatever worship yields fruit,
four times that is declared
in the waters of the river <s>Karatoyā</s>.
In the waters of <s>Karatoyā</s>, O <s>Devī</s>,
worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> is especially meritorious,
yet even more abundant is the fruit
from the worship of <s>Śiva</s> and <s>Śakti</s> together.
At the beginning of the month of <s>Karkaṭaka</s> (Cancer), O <s>Devī</s>,
for three days the <s>Gaṅgā</s> is in her menses,
and all rivers carry red waters,
as does the <s>Karatoyā</s>.
This auspicious <s>Sundarī</s> (beautiful one), O <s>Devī</s>,
is known to carry pure water always.
Those who always bathe therein
and always make offerings of water,
what more need be said, O <s>Deveśī</s> (Queen of the Gods)?
Liberation stands in their hands.
Wondrous is the glory of this water,
born from my very hand,
it is holy and removes the sins of men,
and grants liberation through bathing and drinking.
If one resides on the bank
of the river <s>Karatoyā</s>,
that residence equals one in <s>Vārāṇasī</s>,
and the person is freed from sins.
On the bank of <s>Karajā</s>, O Lord,
worship fulfills all purposes.
Compared to worship done elsewhere, O <s>Devī</s>,
there is no doubt of this, O beautiful one.
Those who die with the water
of <s>Karatoyā</s> in their belly,
for them there is liberation without doubt,
for as long as fourteen <s>Indras</s> reign.
And having attained knowledge there itself,
liberation shall be absolute and pure.
The waters of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and of <s>Karajā</s>
here, O beautiful one,
are holy and remove all sins,
the supreme purifier on earth.
One whose bones, hair, and other remains
fall into <s>Karajā</s>, O practitioner of austerities,
for that person there shall be heaven
for as long as fourteen <s>Indras</s> reign.
On the western bank of <s>Karatoyā</s>,
the <s>Jāhnavī</s> (Ganges) flows always,
especially where the reddish soil
is found, which grants liberation.
On the western bank of <s>Karatoyā</s>,
where the reddish soil is found,
the field of liberation is proclaimed,
which destroys the greatest sins.
The water of <s>Karatoyā</s> is holy,
purifying and rare upon the earth.
Having bathed throughout the entire month of <s>Māgha</s>,
one goes to the city of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
On the bank of the river <s>Karatoyā</s>,
one who is devoted to Vedic worship and recitation,
merely by feeding <s>Brāhmaṇas</s>,
obtains the fruit of an <s>Aśvamedha</s> (horse sacrifice).
Especially in the city of <s>Pauṇḍra</s>,
the merit becomes ten million times ten million-fold.
By feeding even a single <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>,
one obtains the fruit of all sacrifices.
Through <s>japa</s> (recitation), <s>homa</s> (fire offerings), and likewise gifts,
worship, <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rites), and other rituals,
the merit becomes ten million times ten million-fold
in the sacred land of <s>Pauṇḍra</s>, O beautiful one.
Those who wear a <s>tilaka</s> (forehead mark)
made from the clay of <s>Karatoyā</s>,
bearing the form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, are freed from sins;
there is no doubt about this.
Between <s>Skanda</s> and <s>Govinda</s> (temples)
lies hidden the city of <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.
Merely by ascending there,
a person becomes <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
This sacred land extends five <s>krośas</s> (leagues)
in all directions, as proclaimed.
Within that, this inner area
is but one <s>krośa</s>, O <s>Maheśvarī</s> (Great Goddess),
the most secret of sacred lands,
where the sage <s>Bhārgava</s> abides.

children.text: paśor jñānaṃ kathayati guhas tadgṛhe tāmracūḍo
children.translated_text: <s>Guha</s> (Skanda) imparts knowledge to creatures; in his temple the red-crested cock (crows),
a tall golden <s>Surabhi</s> (wish-fulfilling cow) is fashioned, the staff grows, and bones turn to stone,

children.text: kheṣu chhattraṃ na phaṇati phaṇī dvisvaro jīvalokaḥ
children.translated_text: an umbrella appears in the skies, the serpent does not hiss, a dual-voiced being lives,
a well becomes an island, gold rains down — such are the wonders of the <s>Pauṇḍra</s> sacred land.

children.text: proccā bhūmir bhavati taruṇaḥ snānataḥ kāmyakuṇḍe
children.translated_text: The ground rises high; one becomes youthful from bathing in <s>Kāmyakuṇḍa</s> (the Pool of Desire),

children.text: bhogo yajño bhramaṇanaṭanaṃ tatra vākyaṃ hi vedaḥ
children.translated_text: enjoyment itself is sacrifice, wandering and dancing there, and speech is the <s>Veda</s>.
Thus <s>Rāma</s> composed these twenty marks less by one characteristic,
and therefore this <s>Śrīmahāsthāna</s> (Great Sacred Place) is renowned throughout all the worlds.

children.text: snānād yatra nihanti pāpanicayaṃ śrīpāṇitoyā nadī
children.translated_text: The river <s>Śrīpāṇitoyā</s> (Sacred Hand-Water) destroys heaps of sin by bathing,
human bones resting in her waters all turn to stone,

children.text: devas tārakamārako 'pi nitarāṃ jñānaṃ dadāty adbhutaṃ
children.translated_text: the god <s>Tārakamāraka</s> (Slayer of Tāraka, i.e., Skanda) bestows wondrous knowledge,

children.text: kaupaṃ yat paya eva tailavipulaṃ pauṇḍraṃ puraḥ pātu vaḥ
children.translated_text: and the well whose water is verily abundant as oil — may the city of <s>Pauṇḍra</s> protect you.

body.text: COMM.: c. adbhutaṃ: corr., adbhūtaṃ ed.

body.translated_text: Thus ends the Glory of the <s>Pauṇḍra</s> Sacred Land in the <s>Uttarapauṇḍrakhaṇḍa</s>.

children.translated_text: Listen, O sages all,
to the greatness of that water
and on this bank of the <s>Bāhudā</s> (river),
the water that removes all impurity.
Whether it be the <s>Gaṅgā</s> or the <s>Karatoyā</s>,
there is no distinction here.
The <s>Gaṅgā</s> situated on the head of <s>Hara</s> (Śiva) —
that other one has flowed from his hand.
O <s>Karatoyā</s>, ever-flowing,
best of rivers, well-renowned,
you constantly flood the <s>Pauṇḍra</s> [lands];
O one born from the hand, remove [our] sin.
With this <s>mantra</s> indeed one should bathe
in the auspicious water of the <s>Karatoyā</s>.
No river exists of form equal to yours;
free from impurity, for you are ever-young.
Blessed are you, holy are you, best of rivers;
obeisance to you, O one born from the hand of <s>Śrīkaṇṭha</s> (Śiva).
By bathing, this water born from the hand destroys sins;
the Lord <s>Tārakāri</s> (enemy of Tāraka, i.e. Śiva) bestows knowledge here.
<s>Bāhudā</s> [she is called] because of the generous giving
of the sage <s>Likhita</s> in ancient times.
Ever-flowing, greatly meritorious,
bearing cool waters, auspicious.
<s>Ṛṣis</s> and sages indeed —
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>, the great sage,
<s>Aśvatthāmā</s>, the foremost among monkeys (Hanumān),
<s>Vāsudeva</s> himself, the all-pervading Lord,
the four-faced one (<s>Brahmā</s>), the five-faced one (<s>Śiva</s>),
the elephant-faced one (<s>Gaṇeśa</s>), and the six-faced one (<s>Kārttikeya</s>) —
all of them on the western side,
on the bank of the <s>Karatoyā</s> river,
dwell for the sake of <s>tapas</s> (austerity),
desiring the waters of the ever-flowing [river].
Free from impurity, greatly meritorious,
especially so when the sun is in Leo (<s>Siṃha</s>).
O beautiful one, merely by reaching
the waters of the <s>Karatoyā</s> river,
bathing and offering <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) are obligatory;
then crossing to the other shore is prescribed.
For one who crosses to the other shore without bathing,
there would be destruction of previous merit.
Having bathed and drunk the water,
one should not defile either bank.
The <s>Pauṇḍra</s> land, greatly meritorious,
flooded by waters born from the hand [of Śiva],
merely by bathing in those waters,
increases the pleasure of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
To the north of the <s>Pauṇḍra</s> land,
at a distance of two <s>yojanas</s>,
there dwells the goddess <s>Caṇḍikā</s>,
where the soil is reddish.
Merely by praying at her stream,
horses and mansions
the goddess <s>Caṇḍikā</s> bestows
on the bank of the <s>Karatoyā</s> river.
Oh, by the greatness of this sacred land,
the sin of <s>brahmahatyā</s> (killing a Brahmin) is removed.

body.text: COMM.: a. taddhāre: is this the intended reading? Or taddhari? The printing is unclear.

children.translated_text: Sacred water touched by <s>Cāṇḍālas</s> and outcastes
is not purifying —
except for the <s>Gaṅgā</s> born from the hand,
and the waters of the <s>Narmadā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>.
Even with water brought in vessels,
those people who bathe
are released from the mass of sins without exception —
there is no doubt about this.
Whether knowingly
or unknowingly, a person who bathes in the water of the <s>Karatoyā</s>
attains the world of <s>Brahmā</s>,
having destroyed the sins of the day.
Even unknowingly, those humans who
drink even once the water born from the hand [of Śiva],
though of wicked conduct, become
freed from sin.
Here, in the city of <s>Pauṇḍra</s> itself, is the attainment of the goals of human life;
<s>Vārāṇasī</s> is indeed the supreme misfortune of men [by comparison].
There indeed is the abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s> and all sacrifice,
knowledge, various forms of <s>samādhi</s>, and the attainment perfected by <s>japa</s> (chanting).
<s>Kṛṣṇaveṇī</s>, <s>Tāmraparṇī</s>,
<s>Sarayū</s>, and <s>Gaṇḍakī</s> likewise,
the holy one born from the foot of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
<s>Yamunā</s> and <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
<s>Kāverī</s>, <s>Kauśikī</s>, <s>Candrabhāgā</s>,
and <s>Ciravallabhī</s>,
<s>Svarṇā</s>, <s>Campā</s>, <s>Vetravatī</s>,
and also <s>Ātreyī</s>, the reborn one,
<s>Vipāpā</s> and <s>Vipāśā</s>,
<s>Citrā</s> and <s>Citrotpalā</s> likewise,
<s>Gotamī</s>, <s>Gomukhī</s>, <s>Revā</s>,
and also <s>Cirasarasvatī</s>,
all the rivers dwelling on the earth,
all the collections of waters, O dear one —
the waters of all these rivers
are ever present in the water of the <s>Karatoyā</s>.
Having recited this in the island of <s>Pauṇḍra</s>,
the sage <s>Śrīvīra</s> of the <s>Bhārgava</s> lineage,
having circumambulated the <s>Pauṇḍra</s> [land],
is released from the sin of <s>brahmahatyā</s>.
He who, being pure, reads this
<s>māhātmya</s> (glorification) of the great <s>tīrtha</s> (sacred ford) of the <s>Karatoyā</s>,
at the three twilight junctions or at one twilight junction,
or the person who listens to it —
having enjoyed all pleasures here,
with mind fixed upon that [holy place],
after death he goes to the supreme abode
which removes all impurities.

body.text: COMM.: In this GRETIL version verse 85 had to be divided for technical reasons; it should be read as one verse.
ity uttarapauṇḍrakhaṇḍe sūtaśaunakasaṃvāde paraśurāmaviracitaṃ karatoyāmāhātmyaṃ samāptam |
body.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>Karatoyāmāhātmya</s> (Glorification of the Karatoyā) composed by <s>Paraśurāma</s>, in the dialogue between <s>Sūta</s> and <s>Śaunaka</s>, in the <s>Uttarapauṇḍrakhaṇḍa</s> (Later Section on Pauṇḍra).
